{
  "verdict": "fix",
  "issues": [
    "Omitting pagination and filtering for GET /v1/tasks creates an unbounded response risk that will degrade performance and break clients as data scales.",
    "Relying on client-side validation for UUIDs and date formats is a critical security and data integrity flaw; servers must validate all incoming payloads to prevent malformed data injection.",
    "The specification lacks concurrency control mechanisms (e.g., ETags or If-Match headers) for PATCH and DELETE, increasing the risk of race conditions and lost updates.",
    "The stated tradeoff regarding client-side validation for dates contradicts the schema, which excludes created_at and updated_at from request bodies, making client validation irrelevant for those fields.",
    "No authentication or authorization strategy is defined, leaving all CRUD endpoints exposed to unauthorized access and data manipulation."
  ],
  "suggestions": [
    "Add limit/offset or cursor-based pagination parameters to GET /v1/tasks and define a standardized paginated response envelope.",
    "Mandate server-side validation for all request payloads, including UUID format and ISO 8601 compliance, using framework-level middleware or validation libraries.",
    "Implement optimistic concurrency control by requiring ETag generation and If-Match header validation for PATCH and DELETE operations.",
    "Clarify that created_at and updated_at are strictly server-generated immutable fields and remove the contradictory client-side validation tradeoff.",
    "Define a baseline authentication mechanism (e.g., Bearer token or API key) and specify required authorization headers for all endpoints."
  ]
}
